L11@P0: Summary. This article contains an elementary constructive proof of resolution of
L12@P0: singularities in characteristic zero. Our proof applies in particular to schemes of
L13@P0: finite type and to analytic spaces (so we recover the great theorems of Hironaka).
L14@P0: We introduce a discrete local invariant invX (a) whose maximum locus determines
L15@P0: a smooth centre of blowing up, leading to desingularization. To define invX , we
L16@P0: need only to work with a category of local-ringed spaces X =(|X|, OX ) satisfying
L17@P0: certain natural conditions. If a ∈|X|, then invX (a) depends only on Ob
L18@P0: X,a . More
L19@P0: generally, invX is defined inductively after any sequence of blowings-up whose
L20@P0: centres have only normal crossings with respect to the exceptional divisors and lie
L21@P0: in the constant loci of invX (·). The paper is self-contained and includes detailed
L22@P0: examples. One of our goals is that the reader understand the desingularization
L23@P0: theorem, rather than simply “know” it is true.

L46@P1: Chapter I. Introduction
L47@P1: This article contains an elementary constructive proof of resolution of singularities in characteristic zero. k will denote a field of characteristic zero throughout
L48@P1: the paper. Our proof applies to a scheme X of finite type over k, or to an analytic
L49@P1: space X over k (in the case that k has a complete valuation); we recover, in particular, the great theorems of Hironaka [H1,2], [AHV1,2]. But our work neither
L50@P1: was conceived nor is written in the modern language of algebraic geometry. We
L51@P1: introduce a discrete local invariant invX (a) whose maximum locus determines
L52@P1: a centre of blowing up, leading to desingularization. To define invX , we need
L53@P1: only to work with a category A of local-ringed spaces X =(|X|, OX ) over k
L54@P1: satisfying certain mild conditions (Remark 1.5), although further restrictions on
L55@P1: A are needed for global resolution of singularities.
L56@P1: If a ∈|X|, then invX (a) depends only on the completed local ring Ob
L57@P1: X,a .
L58@P1: In general, invX is defined recursively over a sequence of blowings-up whose
L59@P1: centres have only normal crossings with respect to the exceptional divisors and lie
L60@P1: in the constant loci of invX . (See (1.2).) invX takes only finitely many maximum
L61@P1: values (at least locally). Moreover, its maximum locus has only normal crossings
L62@P1: and each of its local components extends to a global smooth subspace, justifying
L63@P1: the philosophy that “a sufficiently good local choice [of centre of blowing-up]
L64@P1: should globalize automatically” [BM4].
L65@P1: (0.1) Our desingularization algorithm applies to the following classes of
L66@P1: spaces:

L69@P1: type over k to their k-rational points |X|k . (Such spaces might be the natural
L70@P1: object of study when our main interest lies in the k-rational points; e.g., for real
L71@P1: algebraic varieties.)
L72@P1: (2) Analytic. Real or complex analytic spaces (cf. [H2], [AHV1,2]). p-adic
L73@P1: analytic spaces in the sense of Serre [Se] or Berkovich [Ber].

L11@P6: Many traditional books in complex and algebraic geometry focus in varieties,
L12@P6: whereas in the present book we focus on neighborhoods of varieties embedded in
L13@P6: other higher dimensional varieties, and in particular those which are negatively embedded. For this we have mainly expanded Hans Grauert’s remarkable 1962 article.
L14@P6: In order to make the book suitable for a course in complex geometry we also provide many preliminaries from Gunning’s 1991 three volumes books. We go further
L15@P6: and study germs of holomorphic foliations in a neighborhood of a variety, and this
L16@P6: takes us to new research topics. A basic knowledge in complex analysis in one variable and algebraic topology is useful for a smooth reading of the present book. The
L17@P6: present book is an expanded version of the monograph “ Neighborhoods of Analytic
L18@P6: Varieties” jointly written with Cesar Camacho in 2003. ´
